sg.ra: Closest and most direct view of the stage at Shubert Theatre, with the fullest sound. The standard top pick for any show here.
An elevated, full-stage view with no orchestra-level neck-craning — especially strong for shows with big staging or choreography.
A modest side angle on the stage but still close and clear — a reliable choice when center seats are sold out.
Farther from the stage than center orchestra — less up-close, but the sound still carries well.
Shubert Theatre's own seating notes flag obstructed or distant views from the far side balcony/mezzanine — worth avoiding unless it's the only option.

vs.sum: The Shubert Theatre offers good sightlines with minimal obstructions, though some seats may require leaning forward for a full view. The sound quality is generally consistent and clear. While legroom is limited in some areas, the theater's historic charm and central location add to its appeal. Facilities are average, with typical lines at restrooms and concessions.

acc.note: 7 wheelchair spaces in Orchestra. No wheelchair-accessible restrooms (available across street).
